deep.reconstruction:
Context (from the neighbouring pages): X → S is a morphism and P^* is the cosimplicial O_X-algebra of formal neighbourhoods of the diagonal. Its terms are P^i = 'O of the formal completion of X in X^{i+1}_S' (fibre power over S), defined functorially as P(I) for finite nonempty sets I. P^i is a pro-object, the system of the infinitesimal neighbourhoods of order n. Its coface maps are the various 'projection' structures. In the affine case X = Spec A, S = Spec k, the global sections are completions of A^{⊗(i+1)}.

The previous page introduced the shifted object SP, with (SP)^i = P^{i+1}. It also introduced the map α: P^* → SP^*, x_0⊗…⊗x_i ↦ x_0⊗…⊗x_i⊗1.

This page (section 2): let M be an O_X-module. Words crossed out first ('(M, ∇_M)', 'stratifié plein') suggest Grothendieck first wanted M with extra structure, then decided to start from a bare module. He sets P^i[M] := P^i ⊗_{O_X} M, where P^i is viewed as an O_X-algebra via its 'external right' structure (the last projection). In modern terms P^i[M] is the completed pullback p_{last}^* M on the formal neighbourhood of the diagonal in X^{i+1}.

He stresses that the tensor product must be read in the category of pro-objects, as P^i itself is. Only under exceptional finiteness hypotheses is it reasonable to replace the pro-sheaves P^i and P^i[M] by honest sheaves, namely their projective limits. The hypotheses are roughly: X locally noetherian, Ω^1_{X/S} or X/S of finite type, M of finite type.

P^i[M] is a P^i-module (via the remaining, left factors) and depends functorially on M ∈ Mod(O_X).

The next page completes the construction. Q^i = P^{i+1} (the shifted algebra), and Q^*[M] = Q^* ⊗_{O_X} M is a cosimplicial module over the cosimplicial ring P^*. Section 3 then observes the 'highly special' cartesian property: the Q^i[M] are deduced from one another by base change along the cosimplicial maps P^i → P^j. This prepares the definition of a stratification/crystal as a cartesian cosimplicial module (a descent datum on the formal groupoid), and of de Rham/crystalline cohomology via the associated Čech–Alexander type complexes.

The problem served: preparing the November–December 1967 lectures on crystals by giving a cosimplicial/descent-theoretic definition of stratified modules (crystals on the infinitesimal or stratifying site) and of their cohomology.
errors: No mathematical error. Minor point: when M is not of finite type (or X not noetherian), the projective limit of the pro-system P^i_n ⊗ M differs from the naive completed tensor product. Grothendieck explicitly flags this, which is precisely why he insists on pro-objects; so this is a caveat he made himself, not a gap.
The page breaks off mid-sentence ('Si on prend comme base de M dans ...'); the thread continues on the next page.

ideas.what: Cosimplicial algebra P^* of formal neighbourhoods of the diagonal in X^{i+1}_S (principal parts of infinite order), treated as a pro-object
ideas.modern_name: Formal groupoid / stratifying-site Čech nerve; principal parts P^∞_{X/S}
ideas.where_published: EGA IV §16 (principal parts); 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' in Dix exposés (1968)

ideas.what: P^i[M] = P^i ⊗_{O_X} M via the right structure, as a P^i-module, with the warning that it must be read as a pro-object except under noetherian/finite-type hypotheses
ideas.modern_name: Completed pullback of M to the formal neighbourhood of the diagonal; linearization / Čech–Alexander construction
ideas.where_published: Crystals paper (Dix exposés), in the finite-order version P^n; the pro-object emphasis is close to EGA IV 16 and SGA conventions

ideas.what: Shifted object Q^* = SP^* and the cosimplicial P^*-module Q^*[M], prepared for a cartesian (descent) characterisation of stratifications
ideas.modern_name: Stratifications as cartesian cosimplicial modules (descent data along the formal groupoid); décalage
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Crystals), Berthelot; Illusie's use of décalage
ideas.where_published: Crystals paper, §§ on stratifications (in groupoid language rather than cosimplicial)

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard preparatory definitions for Grothendieck's crystal lectures: principal parts, pullback to the diagonal neighbourhoods, and a cosimplicial module over P^*. The material appears in the Crystals paper and Berthelot's work. The insistence on pro-objects in the non-noetherian case is a sensible caveat, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the crossed-out text is '(M, ∇_M)', with ∇_M struck through; '[-stratifié plein-]' is struck through at the end of line 1 and start of line 2.
'P^{i*}' should be 'P^i'; the asterisk-like marks are struck-through superscripts.
'agissant sur O_X' should probably read 'Algèbre sur O_X' ('considéré comme Algèbre sur O_X par sa structure extérieure-droite').
The bracketed hypothesis is better read as '[p.ex. X/S de type fini (or lisse), X loc. noeth., Ω_{X/S} et M de type fini sur X]'; uncertain, but '$\mathcal{O}_{X/S}$[?]' is likely Ω_{X/S}.

'préfaisceaux à pentes[?] cas' should read something like 'au lieu de profaisceaux à partir [de] ces cas, on remplace les profaisceaux par leurs lim←'. The objects are pro-faisceaux (pro-sheaves), not préfaisceaux.

'sous des conditions exceptionnelles' is correct; the following 'qu'il est raisonnable d'interpréter P^i et P^i[M] comme des faisceaux plutôt que des profaisceaux' should read profaisceaux, not préfaisceaux.
